DI BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dil . ov. h OILG OPINION NO. 08 Ms. RUBELYN AGUILA ZUNIGA Rubelyn28aguila@gmail.com Dear Ms. Zuniga: This refers to your electronic mail dated December 14, 2023, seeking clarifications on whether barangay officials who ran and lost in the recent barangay elections are entitled to 13th month pay and leave credits. Before we categorically answer the foregoing query, we deemed it prudent to clarify that 13th month pay pertains to a mid-year bonus, which is normally granted to entitled or qualified government personnel pursuant to the guidelines issued by the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) not earlier than May 15 of the year. On that note, we surmise that what is being inquired upon is the grant of 14th month pay, or more commonly known as the Year-End Bonus (YEB), which is usually granted to entitled government personnel not earlier than November 15 of the year pursuant to DBM Budget Circular No. 2016-4, dated April, 28, 20161. The grant of a 14th month pay, or YEB, finds its basis in Executive Order No. 201, series of 2016.2 Parenthetically, the guidelines on the grant of YEB are stipulated under DBM Budget Circular No. 2016-4, dated April 28, 2016. Item 7. thereof provides that: "Year-End Bonus and Cash Gift of Barangay Personnel 7.1 As determined by the respective sanggunian, elective or appointive barangay officials or employees who have rendered at least a total or an aggregate of four (4) months of service from January I of the current year and who are still in the service as of October 31 of the same year, may be entitled to the Year-End Bonus equivalent to one (I) month Honorarium received as of October 31 and Cash Gift of P5,ooo. Accordingly, if you have rendered at least a total or aggregate of four (4) months of service from January I of 2023 to October 31 of the same year, you should be entitled to YEB, notwithstanding the 2023 Synchronized Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections, which took place on October 30 per COMELEC Resolution No. 109053. I Updated Rules and Regulations on the Grant of the Year-End Bonus and Cash Gift for FY 2016 and Years Thereafter" 2 "Modifying the Salary Schedule for Civilian Government Personnel and Authorizing the Grant Of Additional Benefits for Both Civilian and Military and Uniformed Personnel." 3 Revised Calendar of Activities and Periods Of Certain Prohibited Acts in Connection with the October 30, 2023 Synchronized Barangay and Sangguniang Elections (BSKE) "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

As to leave credits, we opine in the affirmative. Pursuant to Section 37 of Civil Service Commission (CSC) Memorandum Circular No. 14, series of 19994 "Any official/employee of the government who retires, voluntarily resigns or is separated from the service and who is not otherwise covered by special law, shall be entitled to the commutation of his leave credits exclusive of Saturdays, Sundays and Holidays without limitation and regardless of the period when the credits were earned. " (Emphasis ours) To bolster this, the CSC, in its Resolution No. 01-06735, clarified that accrued leave credits (terminal leave benefits) are considered as earned salaries of the official or employee concerned, and the latter was ruled to be entitled to the same as a matter of course. This opinion shall be without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, By the Authority of the Secretary: VICTOR R.
